idiom_name: opaque-handle constructor function + const function-pointer ops table
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor inheritance, so the Creator/ConcreteCreator pair has no counterpart: the product interface becomes a struct whose first member points to a const table of function pointers, and the factory method becomes a constructor function such as shape_create(enum shape_kind) that selects the table and the concrete constructor at run time (a switch, or a creator-function pointer stored in a creator struct). What replaces the classic structure is therefore the tag dispatch plus the ops table - the caller sees only the opaque struct and never the concrete type. The classic form is not available even in principle, so a hand-written vtable is the only portable route to polymorphic creation; hide the struct definition in the .c file and expose only the constructor, the ops-table entry points and a destroy function.
pitfalls: Returning NULL for an unknown kind is legal but easy to ignore; declare one failure convention (NULL, errno, or an out-parameter status) and check it at every call site.
The ops table must be static const and shared by all instances of a type; a per-instance copy wastes memory and invites accidental mutation of the vtable.
Pair every *_create with a *_destroy honoring the same allocator; mixing malloc/free across a library boundary corrupts the heap.

A struct cast to an incompatible ops table (or a stale ops pointer after realloc) is undefined behaviour with no compiler help; keep the first member exactly one pointer and initialize it in every constructor.
